meta.title: Hunt & Haul
meta.subtitle: An open-world Roblox hunting game. Drive out in your truck, hunt animals and bosses, haul the carcasses and eggs home, shred them for coins, hatch the eggs, and upgrade.

phases.name: World
phases.goal: A walkable, optimized map with the player base laid out.

phases.name: Truck & player
phases.goal: The truck drives the whole map; the player moves and aims.

phases.name: Core loop
phases.goal: Shoot one animal, haul it home, shred it for coins. End to end.

phases.name: Progression & tutorial
phases.goal: Eggs, pets, shop, saving and a tutorial that teaches the loop.

phases.name: Content & social
phases.goal: Full animal roster, bosses, night spawns, co-op.

phases.name: Launch prep
phases.goal: Monetization, UI polish, Roblox rules, marketing, performance, beta.

phases.name: Live ops
phases.goal: Events, updates every 2 to 3 weeks, subscriptions, trading.

root.title: Hunt & Haul
root.summary: The whole product. Every area rolls up into one loop: drive out, hunt, haul back, shred and hatch, upgrade.
deliverables: This roadmap kept up to date
acceptance: A new player can complete the full loop in under 10 minutes
60 FPS on a mid-range PC, 30 FPS on a mid-range phone
risks: Scope creep before the core loop is fun
Map too large for phone memory

children.title: World & map
children.summary: The open world: terrain, mountains, river, road, forests and props, plus the gameplay layout on top of it.
deliverables: Zones and points of interest placed
acceptance: Every zone reachable by truck
No buried or floating assets
risks: Blender to Roblox import limits (2048-stud mesh cap)

children.title: Map creation in Blender
children.summary: AlpineValley_Optimized: 4096 x 4096 studs, 256 terrain chunks, mountain ring, valley floor, road, trails, river, waterfall gorge, barn and farmyard.
acceptance: Each chunk imports under 2048 studs
Ground colour matches the reference clips
risks: Assets placed under the terrain surface
children.notes: Scene audit (Nov 6): River_water and all four bridges sit below the ground surface, and the 04_Waterfall camera is inside the terrain.

children.title: Fix buried river and bridges
children.summary: River_water is at z 1.3 where the ground is about 31. Bridge_-90, Bridge_172, Bridge_-390 and StoneBridge top out below the ground.
deliverables: River channel carved into the terrain
acceptance: Every water and bridge object sits above the terrain

children.title: Vegetation pass
children.summary: 1,608 oaks, 833 pines, plus ferns, flowers, dry grass and shrubs. Reduce to a few reusable variants for Roblox.
acceptance: Trees reuse the same MeshId so Roblox instances them
risks: Trees rooted into steep rock on the mountain apron

children.title: Import pipeline
children.summary: Export FBX by category, import with Studio's 3D importer, align to origin, set materials and collision.
deliverables: Terrain, props and trees as separate FBX files
acceptance: Scale is 1:1 (one Blender metre = one stud)
Terrain uses precise collision, decoration uses box or none
risks: The importer rescales meshes over 2048 studs

children.title: Map design (gameplay layer)
children.summary: Where things go and why: base location, hunting zones, boss arenas, roads, and difficulty rising the further you drive from the barn.
deliverables: List of points of interest with coordinates
acceptance: Easy animals within 300 studs of the base
Each boss arena at least 1,000 studs from the base

children.title: Hunting zones
children.summary: Meadow (chickens, rabbits), forest (deer, boar), riverbank (ducks), rocky slopes (goats), gorge and ridges (bosses).
acceptance: Zones don't overlap
Each zone has 8 or more spawn points

children.title: Roads, trails and ramps
children.summary: The road loop plus dirt trails so every zone is drivable, with ramps and jumps for fun.
acceptance: The truck reaches every zone without getting stuck

children.title: Points of interest
children.summary: Hunting stands, ammo caches, dynamite crates, lookout points, the clock tower.

children.title: Boss arenas
children.summary: Three to five set-piece spots: waterfall gorge, clock tower, ridge clearing, deep forest.
acceptance: Each arena fits a truck and 4 players

children.title: Map borders and out of bounds
children.summary: Keep players inside the playable map and recover them when things go wrong.
deliverables: Invisible walls along the mountain ring
acceptance: Nobody can leave the map or fall forever

children.title: Navigation aids
children.summary: Help players find their way: radar/compass, a waypoint back to the barn, and a full map screen with zone names.
acceptance: A new player can find the barn again from anywhere

children.title: Lighting and sky
children.summary: Bright cartoon sky with cumulus clouds, warm sun and light atmosphere.
acceptance: Matches the reference clips side by side

children.title: Day and night cycle
children.summary: A slow day/night loop. Some animals only come out at night.
risks: Night too dark on low-brightness phones

children.title: Map performance
children.summary: Streaming, reused meshes, collision rules and a parts budget so the map runs on phones.
deliverables: Budget sheet: triangles and parts per zone
acceptance: Under 1.5 GB client memory on a mid-range phone

children.title: Player base
children.summary: Home: the barn and hut, the square hatching pen, the shredder, truck parking and the spawn.
acceptance: Every player spawns at their own base
risks: Per-player plots on a shared map need clear separation

children.title: Barn and hut
children.summary: The red gambrel barn is already modelled. Add an interior, storage and the spawn point.

children.title: Hatching pen
children.summary: The fenced square next to the barn with egg slots and incubation timers.
acceptance: Timers keep running while the player is offline

children.title: Shredder
children.summary: Drop carcasses in, coins come out. Upgradable speed and payout.
acceptance: Payout matches the animal value table
Runs on the server only

children.title: Truck unloading zone
children.summary: Back the truck in and the cargo moves automatically: carcasses to the shredder, eggs to the pen.

children.title: One plot per player
children.summary: Each player in a server gets their own base. A 'My Plot' button takes you home.
acceptance: Up to 8 plots per server with no overlap

children.title: Base upgrades and decoration
children.summary: More hatch slots, faster shredder, bigger parking, and cosmetic paint and decorations for the barn.
deliverables: Upgrade tiers for pen and shredder

children.title: Player and character
children.summary: The duck avatar, cameras, movement, health, inventory and carrying.

children.title: Duck avatar and animations
children.summary: Idle, walk, run, aim, reload, throw, carry and hurt.

children.title: Camera modes
children.summary: First person for shooting, third person on foot and in the truck.
acceptance: Switches cleanly when getting in and out of the truck

children.title: Movement and stamina
children.summary: Walk, sprint with stamina, jump. Carrying a carcass slows you down.

children.title: Health, death and respawn
children.summary: Aggressive animals and bosses can hurt you. On death you respawn at the base; cargo already on the truck stays there.
acceptance: You never lose loaded cargo by dying

children.title: Inventory and hotbar
children.summary: Weapons, dynamite and one carried item.

children.title: Carrying
children.summary: Pick up a carcass or egg, carry it, and load it onto the truck bed.
acceptance: Only one heavy item carried at a time

children.title: The truck
children.summary: Reuse the existing driving scripts. The truck gets you to the zones and brings the loot home.
deliverables: Drivable truck across the whole map
acceptance: Drives every road and trail
Carries up to 6 items
risks: The existing driving code may assume flat ground

children.title: Driving and physics
children.summary: Port the existing driving files: suspension, grip, acceleration, braking, steering.
acceptance: Climbs map slopes
Doesn't flip on normal turns

children.title: Seats, entering and exiting
children.summary: A driver seat plus passenger seats for co-op.

children.title: Cargo bed
children.summary: Slots for carcasses and eggs that stack visibly. Heavy loads slow the truck.
deliverables: Items attach to the bed when loaded
acceptance: Cargo stays on during jumps

children.title: Dashboard and radar
children.summary: A radar like the reference clip, speed, and cargo count.

children.title: Flip recovery and respawn
children.summary: A button to flip the truck upright, and respawning it at the base.

children.title: Truck upgrades
children.summary: Engine, tyres and a bigger bed.

children.title: Truck skins
children.summary: Paint jobs and decals. A cosmetic money-maker.

children.title: Weapons and combat
children.summary: Guns driven by a config table, dynamite, ammo, and how hitting things feels.
acceptance: Shooting feels responsive at 150 ms ping

children.title: Gun framework
children.summary: One module. Every gun is a config entry: damage, fire rate, spread, recoil, magazine, reload time, range falloff.
deliverables: Pistol, shotgun and rifle to start
acceptance: A new gun can be added with config only

children.title: Aiming and scopes
children.summary: Hip fire, aiming down sights, and a scope overlay for the rifle.

children.title: Hit detection
children.summary: The client raycasts so it feels instant; the server re-checks distance, line of sight and fire rate.
acceptance: Hits through walls and shots faster than the fire rate are rejected

children.title: Ammo and reloading
children.summary: Ammo per gun type, bought in the shop or found in caches on the map.

children.title: Dynamite
children.summary: Throw arc, fuse, explosion damage in a radius, and knockback.
acceptance: Doesn't damage the map

children.title: Combat feel
children.summary: Muzzle flash, tracers, hit markers, impact particles, screen shake and sound.

children.title: Melee bat
children.summary: A fallback weapon, as in the reference clip.

children.title: Weapon skins
children.summary: Cosmetic skins for guns.

children.title: Animals and bosses
children.summary: What you hunt: the roster, spawning, behaviour, drops, rare spawns and boss fights.
risks: Too many active animals hurts server performance

children.title: Animal roster
children.summary: Tiers from common to legendary. Each animal has HP, speed, damage, coin value, egg type and zone.
deliverables: Roster table. Start with chicken, rabbit, deer and boar
children.notes: Suggested tiers: Common (chicken, rabbit), Uncommon (duck, goat), Rare (deer, boar), Epic (bull, bison), Legendary (night-only animals).

children.title: Spawner
children.summary: Caps per zone, respawn timers, rarity rolls, and despawning far from players.
acceptance: Fewer than 60 active animals per server

children.title: Behaviour
children.summary: Wander, graze, flee when shot at; aggressive types charge.

children.title: Death, carcass and egg drop
children.summary: On a kill the animal ragdolls into a carcass you can carry, and may drop an egg.
acceptance: Carcasses stay for 3 minutes

children.title: Headshots
children.summary: Extra damage for headshots.

children.title: Rare and night spawns
children.summary: Rare animals with a server-wide announcement; some only appear at night.

children.title: Boss fights
children.summary: Unique models, attack phases, arena trigger, health bar, big rewards and a rare egg, with a server-wide cooldown.
deliverables: A boss framework for the rest
acceptance: 4 players can beat the first boss in 3 to 5 minutes
children.notes: Ideas: a giant boar in the forest, an alpha moose in the gorge, a mega goose by the river.

children.title: Loot and progression
children.summary: Coins come in, upgrades go out. The numbers that make the loop feel good.
acceptance: First upgrade within 5 minutes of play
risks: Inflation if bosses pay too much

children.title: Shred values
children.summary: Coins per carcass by animal, rarity and weight.

children.title: Economy tuning sheet
children.summary: Model coins per hour at each stage, and match income (sources) against spending (sinks).
deliverables: Spreadsheet with income and price curves
acceptance: Every upgrade tier is 10 to 30 minutes of play apart

children.title: Eggs
children.summary: Egg rarities, hatch times and what can come out of each egg.

children.title: Pets and buffs
children.summary: Hatched pets follow you and give buffs like speed, damage or extra coins. Equip up to 3.

children.title: Shop
children.summary: Guns, ammo, dynamite, truck upgrades and barn upgrades for coins.

children.title: Levels and XP
children.summary: XP from kills unlocks new zones and guns.

children.title: Rebirth
children.summary: Reset progress for a permanent multiplier, for long-term players.

children.title: Index (collection book)
children.summary: Every animal, egg and pet you have found.

children.title: Tutorial and first session
children.summary: The first five minutes decide whether a new player stays. Teach the loop by playing it once, with arrows pointing the way.
acceptance: 70% of new players finish the tutorial
First shred within 3 minutes, first upgrade within 5
risks: A long or wordy tutorial makes players leave

children.title: Loading screen and spawn
children.summary: A short branded loading screen that preloads key assets, then a quick camera sweep of the valley.
acceptance: Playable within 10 seconds on a phone

children.title: Guided tutorial steps
children.summary: Play the whole loop once with one goal on screen at a time.
deliverables: 1. Grab your first gun at the barn
3. Drive to the meadow (follow the arrow)
5. Pick up the carcass and the egg
8. Drop the carcass in the shredder
9. Put the egg in the hatching pen
acceptance: Each step shows one short line of text, no paragraphs

children.title: Arrows, highlights and prompts
children.summary: A trail or arrow to the next goal, a glow on the object to use, and big button prompts on mobile.

children.title: Skip and replay
children.summary: Returning players skip it automatically. Anyone can replay it from Settings.

children.title: Completion reward
children.summary: A free starter egg and some coins for finishing.

children.title: Tips in context
children.summary: One-time tips the first time something happens: first boss, first night, first rare animal, truck full.

children.title: Tutorial funnel analytics
children.summary: Log each tutorial step so you can see exactly where new players drop off.

children.title: Retention and live ops
children.summary: Reasons to come back tomorrow and next week: rewards, goals, events and regular updates.
acceptance: Day 1 retention above 25%, day 7 above 8%

children.title: Daily login rewards
children.summary: A 7-day streak calendar with a bigger prize on day 7.

children.title: Daily and weekly quests
children.summary: Short goals like 'Shred 10 rabbits' or 'Beat a boss' that give coins and XP.

children.title: Badges and achievements
children.summary: Roblox badges for milestones: first kill, first boss, first legendary, rebirth.

children.title: Leaderboards
children.summary: Most coins, bosses beaten and rarest pets. A board at spawn plus a menu tab.

children.title: Codes
children.summary: Redeemable codes shared on social channels and at update launches. Checked on the server, with expiry dates.

children.title: Group and favourite rewards
children.summary: A small bonus for joining the Roblox group; gentle reminders to like and favourite.

children.title: Limited-time events
children.summary: Holiday animals, double-coin weekends and event eggs.
deliverables: Event framework that turns on by date

children.title: Update cadence and update log
children.summary: Ship an update every 2 to 3 weeks; show what changed on a board in game.

children.title: Offline progress
children.summary: Eggs keep hatching while you're away.

children.title: Social and multiplayer
children.summary: Playing together: co-op hunts, friend bonuses, private servers and trading.

children.title: Co-op hunting
children.summary: Ride in a friend's truck, share boss loot, and see each other on the radar.

children.title: Friend boost
children.summary: Extra coins for playing in a server with friends, like the 'Friend Boost' in the reference game.

children.title: Private servers
children.summary: Roblox private servers for groups who want to play alone.

children.title: Chat and emotes
children.summary: Roblox text chat plus a few duck emotes.

children.title: Pet trading
children.summary: Trade pets with other players through a two-sided confirm screen.
acceptance: Both players confirm; nothing can change after confirming
risks: Scams and duplication exploits if built carelessly

children.title: Monetization
children.summary: How the game earns Robux without feeling pay-to-win: time savers, convenience and cosmetics.
deliverables: Store with passes, products and cosmetics
acceptance: Free players can reach every zone and boss

children.title: Strategy and price ladder
children.summary: What to sell and at what price. Sell speed, convenience and looks, never power over other players.
deliverables: List of every offer with its price
acceptance: Every offer has a free way to get the same result more slowly

children.title: Game passes
children.summary: One-time purchases that last forever.
deliverables: VIP (chat tag, VIP area at the barn, small luck bonus)
acceptance: Ownership is checked every time a player joins

children.title: Developer products
children.summary: Things you can buy more than once.

children.title: Robux eggs
children.summary: Eggs bought with Robux. Roblox counts these as paid random items, which come with rules.
deliverables: Odds shown on every Robux egg
Hidden in regions where paid random items aren't allowed
acceptance: Checked with PolicyService before showing
risks: Breaking the paid random item rules can get the game taken down

children.title: Starter pack and limited offers
children.summary: A one-time discounted bundle offered after the tutorial, plus timed offers during events.

children.title: Cosmetic shop
children.summary: Truck skins, gun skins and duck hats.

children.title: Roblox Premium perks and payouts
children.summary: Roblox pays creators based on how long Premium members play. Give Premium players a small perk, such as 10% more coins.

children.title: Experience subscription
children.summary: A monthly subscription with daily coins and an exclusive cosmetic.

children.title: Purchase handling
children.summary: Grant purchases safely: save first, grant once, never twice, and keep a purchase history.
deliverables: ProcessReceipt handler that is safe to call twice
acceptance: No lost or duplicated purchases in testing

children.title: Store screen
children.summary: A clear Robux store tab with honest prices and no tricks.

children.title: Revenue tracking
children.summary: Track which offers sell and where players first spend.

children.title: UI and settings
children.summary: Everything on screen: HUD, menus, settings, accessibility, mobile and console.
acceptance: Everything is usable on a phone

children.title: UI style guide
children.summary: One visual language: fonts, button styles, and a colour for each rarity.

children.title: HUD
children.summary: Ammo, health, coins, cargo count and compass.

children.title: Menus
children.summary: Shop, index, inventory, pets, quests, rebirth.

children.title: Settings menu
children.summary: Music and sound volume, graphics quality, mouse and touch sensitivity, field of view, invert look, replay tutorial.

children.title: Accessibility
children.summary: Scalable text, rarity shown with labels as well as colour, and reduced screen shake.

children.title: Mobile controls
children.summary: Buttons for fire, aim, throw and drive, sized for thumbs.

children.title: Gamepad and console
children.summary: Controller support for Xbox and PlayStation players.

children.title: Notifications
children.summary: Boss spawned, shop restocked, egg hatched.

children.title: Tech and data
children.summary: How the game is built and how player data stays safe.
acceptance: No data loss across 1,000 test sessions

children.title: Code structure
children.summary: Server and client modules, shared config, naming rules, version control.

children.title: Client and server events
children.summary: RemoteEvents for shooting, damage, loot and purchases. The server always decides.

children.title: Saving player data
children.summary: Coins, inventory, pets, egg timers, upgrades, index and rebirths. Autosave, session locking and versioned data.
acceptance: Rejoining on another server never loses or duplicates items

children.title: Anti-exploit
children.summary: Server-side checks for damage, speed, teleporting and purchases.

children.title: Test and live places
children.summary: A separate test place, a publishing checklist and backups.

children.title: Error logging
children.summary: Capture script errors from live servers so bugs get found fast.

children.title: Analytics events
children.summary: Custom events, funnels and economy events through Roblox analytics.

children.title: Audio
children.summary: Ambience, weapons, animals, music and interface sounds.

children.title: Ambience
children.summary: Birds, wind and river, changing by zone.

children.title: Weapon and animal sounds
children.summary: Each gun, explosions, animal calls and hit reactions.

children.title: Music
children.summary: An exploration loop and a boss theme.

children.title: Interface sounds
children.summary: Coins, purchases, hatching and level-up.

children.title: Safety and Roblox rules
children.summary: Stay within Roblox's rules so the game is never taken down and gets the right age rating.
acceptance: Content maturity questionnaire submitted before launch
risks: Hunting with blood effects can raise the age rating

children.title: Content maturity questionnaire
children.summary: Roblox asks about violence and blood to set the age label. Decide how much blood the game shows.
deliverables: Option to tone down blood effects

children.title: Text filtering
children.summary: Any text players type, like pet names, goes through Roblox's text filter.

children.title: Region checks
children.summary: Use PolicyService to hide paid random items and social links where they aren't allowed.

children.title: Data deletion requests
children.summary: When Roblox sends a right-to-erasure request, delete that player's saved data.

children.title: Reports and bans
children.summary: A ban list for exploiters and a way to act on reports.

children.title: Marketing and launch
children.summary: Getting players in the door: the game page, community channels, ads and creators.

children.title: Icon, thumbnails and trailer
children.summary: A clear icon, 3 to 5 thumbnails showing the loop, and a short trailer.
acceptance: Icon readable at small size

children.title: Game name, description and genre
children.summary: A searchable name, a short description of the loop, and the right genre tags.

children.title: Roblox group and Discord
children.summary: A group for rewards and announcements, and a Discord for codes and feedback.

children.title: Roblox ads
children.summary: Sponsored ads through Roblox Ads Manager, small budgets first to test thumbnails.

children.title: YouTube and TikTok creators
children.summary: Send early access and codes to creators who play hunting and simulator games.

children.title: Launch timing
children.summary: Release on a Friday afternoon and ship updates before weekends.

children.title: Testing and release
children.summary: Performance targets, playtests, beta and the soft launch.

children.title: Performance pass
children.summary: 60 FPS on a mid-range PC, 30 FPS on a mid-range phone, within the memory budget.

children.title: Playtests
children.summary: Weekly internal sessions from Phase 3 onward. Track time to first upgrade.

children.title: Closed beta
children.summary: A small group of outside testers before launch.

children.title: Bug tracking
children.summary: One list of bugs with severity, owner and status.

children.title: Soft launch
children.summary: Public release with a small push, then improve based on the numbers.
